facts.text: The README is a setup guide for a UR10e robotic arm with a Robotiq 2F140 gripper, integrated with Isaac Sim.
The README lists two control strategies: Mock Components, and topic-based ROS 2 control with Isaac Sim.
The ROS 2 devcontainer feature line names ROS 2 Humble with all dependencies.
examples.py imports control_msgs.action.FollowJointTrajectory.
examples.py lists the six controlled joints as shoulder_pan_joint, shoulder_lift_joint, elbow_joint, wrist_1_joint, wrist_2_joint and wrist_3_joint, in that order.
examples.py creates a FollowJointTrajectory action client on the absolute /scaled_joint_trajectory_controller/follow_joint_trajectory endpoint.
examples.py also names the absolute /controller_manager/switch_controller service.
examples.py treats a trajectory as successful when the result error_code equals FollowJointTrajectory.Result.SUCCESSFUL.
xbox_control.py imports sensor_msgs.msg.JointState.
xbox_control.py subscribes to the absolute /joint_states topic with a JointState callback.
ur_robotiq_control.launch.py starts controller_manager's ros2_control_node only when use_fake_hardware is true.
The same launch starts ur_robot_driver's ur_ros2_control_node unless use_fake_hardware is true.
The launch spawns robotiq_gripper_controller unless use_fake_hardware is true, and robotiq_gripper_joint_trajectory_controller when it is true, both against /controller_manager.
The launch's controller spawners pass --controller-manager /controller_manager.
The launch spawns forward_position_controller and forward_gripper_position_controller inactive.
The launch's initial joint-controller spawner addresses the controller manager as /controller_manager.
The controllers_file launch argument defaults to ur_robotiq_controllers.yaml.
The tf_prefix launch argument defaults to an empty string.
The use_fake_hardware launch argument defaults to false and is described as starting the robot with fake hardware that mirrors commands to its states.
The initial_joint_controller launch argument defaults to scaled_joint_trajectory_controller.
The activate_joint_controller launch argument defaults to true.
ur_robotiq_controllers.yaml declares joint_trajectory_controller, scaled_joint_trajectory_controller, the forward position and velocity controllers and the Robotiq gripper controllers.
scaled_joint_trajectory_controller is configured for the six arm joints with a position command interface, position and velocity state interfaces, and a speed_scaling state interface name.
forward_position_controller is configured for the same six arm joints.
The ur10e joint_limits.yaml writes min_position and max_position with the !degrees tag (shoulder joints and wrists 360, elbow 180).
ScaledJointTrajectoryController includes joint_trajectory_controller/joint_trajectory_controller.hpp.
ScaledJointTrajectoryController extends JointTrajectoryController and overrides state_interface_configuration, on_activate, update and on_init; on_deactivate is not among them.
The scaled controller's scaling_factor_ member defaults to 1.0.
state_interface_configuration appends speed_scaling_interface_name when that name is non-empty.
on_activate searches the state interfaces already assigned to the controller for the speed-scaling name, logs an error when that search misses, and then calls JointTrajectoryController::on_activate.
When use_fake_hardware is true, ur_macro.xacro includes ur.ros2_control.xacro.
The fake-hardware ros2_control plugin in that description is mock_components/GenericSystem.

Inside the block omitted for sim_gazebo and sim_ignition, the description declares gpio speed_scaling with state interface speed_scaling_factor and parameter initial_speed_scaling_factor 1. The comment says the following are joints used only for testing with fake hardware.
The scaled controller's update reads the scaling factor only when the interface is present, and returns OK immediately while the lifecycle state is inactive.
ur_robotiq_isaac_control.launch.py defaults initial_joint_controller to joint_trajectory_controller.
ur_robotiq_moveit.launch.py says the scaled_joint_trajectory_controller does not work on fake hardware and, when use_fake_hardware is true, sets joint_trajectory_controller as the MoveIt default.
ros2_control_node names its controller manager node controller_manager.
The controller manager creates the list_controllers service with the controller_manager_msgs::srv::ListControllers type under its private name.
The controller manager creates the switch_controller service with the controller_manager_msgs::srv::SwitchController type under its private name.
switch_controller_service_cb passes the request's controllers to activate and deactivate, its strictness, activate_asap and timeout to switch_controller and answers ok only when that returns OK.
switch_controller asks the realtime update loop for the switch and waits for it up to the request's timeout (1 s when it is zero); when the wait times out it clears the request and returns ERROR.
The controller manager's update loop performs a requested switch.
list_controllers fills each ControllerState name from the controller info and its state from the lifecycle label.
SwitchController defines strictness STRICT as 2, under which the switch fails if anything goes wrong, and returns ok when the controllers were switched.
ControllerState's state field is unconfigured, inactive, active or finalized.
On deactivation the trajectory controller aborts an active goal, keeps each position command at its last value, releases its interfaces and drops its stored trajectory.

On activation the trajectory controller takes its current and last commanded state from the command interfaces when set_last_command_interface_value_as_state_on_activation is set and the command read succeeds, and otherwise reads both from the state interfaces.
set_last_command_interface_value_as_state_on_activation defaults to true: the last command interface value is then used as both the current state and the last commanded state on activation.
Reading the state from the command interfaces fails when the controller has a velocity state interface but no velocity command interface with values.
On activation the trajectory controller starts by holding the position of the state it starts from.
set_hold_position commands the positions of the controller's current state (state_current_).
The trajectory controller rejects a new action goal while it is inactive.
Before activation the controller manager claims every individual state interface the controller requested and skips that controller when the claim throws.
claim_state_interface throws when the state interface key does not exist.
GenericSystem records each gpio state interface from the hardware info.
GenericSystem exports each gpio state interface.
GenericSystem initializes a gpio state from the component parameter initial_<interface name> when the interface has no initial_value.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording stand-in with no physics step, trajectory interpolation, controller timing or wall-clock pacing; the placeholder joint samples do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS recording fake (no controller manager and no physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers the declared FollowJointTrajectory action, /joint_states and the two controller-manager services, and it runs no ROS graph, controller manager, Isaac Sim or robot
the action goal is applied instantly to a placeholder six-joint vector; there is no interpolation, timing, feedback, dynamics or controller error behavior
the joint samples are placeholders; a live run must receive /joint_states from the operator's graph and the trajectory result from the operator's scaled_joint_trajectory_controller

this package serves only the fake-hardware path of ur_robotiq_control.launch.py (use_fake_hardware true). The Isaac launch defaults initial_joint_controller to joint_trajectory_controller and is not served. The real ur_ros2_control_node starts unless use_fake_hardware is set and uses the same endpoint names
the MoveIt launch sets joint_trajectory_controller as its default when use_fake_hardware is true; this package does not serve MoveIt, and the e-stop does not show that controller inactive

the stop is the companion controller switch: the fake keeps the scaled controller's lifecycle state, which switch_controller sets and list_controllers reports beside joint_state_broadcaster, and it refuses goals while that controller is inactive; it runs no controller manager or update loop

deactivation keeps each joint's position command at its last value (joint_trajectory_controller.cpp:1069-1075) and drops the stored trajectory; the gripper and the other arm controllers are not stopped
forward_position_controller is loaded inactive and claims the same six arm joints, so another client can activate it after this controller releases its interfaces

the switch waits up to 0.4 s for the controller manager's update loop (controller_manager.cpp:1307-1331; a zero duration becomes 1 s). A timeout answers ok false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held (fails closed). The action timeout_ms is 2000, shorter than the example overlay's 10 s trajectory time

the read-back's list predicate selects the one element named scaled_joint_trajectory_controller (E4): none, two, or a state other than inactive leaves the e-stop unconfirmed. It does not prove joint_trajectory_controller, the forward controllers or the gripper are inactive
any other ROS 2 client of /controller_manager/switch_controller can re-activate the controller after the e-stop; MHS does not watch its state afterwards

the scaled controller requests speed_scaling_interface_name (scaled_joint_trajectory_controller.cpp:63-70). The controller manager claims that state interface before activation and skips the controller when the claim throws (controller_manager.cpp:1653-1681; resource_manager.cpp:743-747). The on_activate log at scaled_joint_trajectory_controller.cpp:91-92 runs only after the interfaces were assigned; it is not a path the manager takes when the interface is missing. On this fake-hardware path, ur_macro.xacro:113-114 includes ur.ros2_control.xacro, which selects mock_components/GenericSystem (:44-48) and declares gpio speed_scaling/speed_scaling_factor with initial_speed_scaling_factor 1 (:160-166). GenericSystem exports that gpio state and initializes it from the initial_ parameter (generic_system.cpp:301-305, :714-726). A description that omits the gpio does not reach on_activate

the deployment's controller_manager and joint_trajectory_controller must be the pinned 2.54.4 and 2.54.1 Humble releases. The lock profile name ros2-humble-gzsim6 is a shared label, not a claim that this package runs Gazebo. rosbridge cannot read those versions. A non-empty tf_prefix is out of scope: this package binds the unprefixed names only

safe_state.description: scaled_joint_trajectory_controller is inactive, as list_controllers read back: its goal was aborted and its trajectory dropped, and each joint's position command keeps its last value; the world keeps running, it is the controller's state and not a measured standstill, other arm controllers and the gripper are not shown inactive, and any client can re-activate it.
